text:
1. Genesis 6 presents both a thoroughly corrupt world and one man who walked with God.
2. The narrator of Genesis 6 does not soften the description of the world's corruption.
3. Genesis 6 says every imagination of the human heart was only evil continually.
4. Genesis 6 says the earth was filled with violence.
5. Genesis 6 says Yahweh was sorry he had made man.
6. Noah is not asked to reform the world.
7. Noah is asked to build.
8. Genesis 6 spends more words on the ark's specifications than on the corruption that makes the ark necessary.
9. The specifications get more attention because Noah builds to a measure he did not set.
10. The ark is defined by its dimensions before it is built from wood.
11. The only thing Genesis 6 says about Noah's part is that he did all that God commanded him.
12. Genesis 6 names Noah as righteous before he acts.
13. In Genesis 6, Noah's righteousness becomes visible as obedience.
14. That obedience is Noah's willingness to build what God says will be needed.
15. God has seen the whole world.
